$comment: From a catalogue action (src/lib/ai/actions.ts) to a workflow, a version
and the node inputs it overrides (Phase 21.2, #101).
THIS FILE AND THE WORKFLOWS ARE THE BLAST RADIUS. Node class names, node
ids and input keys are ComfyUI concepts and they are allowed to exist
here and in workflows/*.json and nowhere else in the repository — not in
src/, not in api/. If ComfyUI is ever replaced, this directory is what
gets rewritten and nothing above it moves. `comfy/pipeline.test.ts`
A parameter that is NOT listed under `params` is fixed by the workflow.
That is a product decision every time, and `fixed` says which decision
and why — an exposed knob nobody explained is how a catalogue stops
matching what the graph actually accepts.

fixed.sampler_name / scheduler: dpmpp_2m + karras. Exposing the sampler would make the catalogue's determinism claim untestable — the same seed on a different sampler is a different image, and the claim is per action, not per request.
fixed.batch_size: One image per job. 21.4 prices a job; a batch would make a job's cost depend on a parameter the ceiling never sees.
fixed.denoise: 1.0 — anything less is image-to-image, which is its own action.

fixed.negativePrompt: Empty. The catalogue does not offer one for this action, and a graph input the product cannot reach is a graph input that drifts.
fixed.cfg: 5 — tuned with the fixed sampler; the two are one setting in practice.
fixed.sampler_name / scheduler: As text-to-image, and for the same reason.

fixed.grow_mask_by: 6 px. A mask that stops exactly at the edge leaves a seam; this is the smallest value that reliably hides one.
fixed.channel: The mask's red channel, so a plain black-and-white PNG works and white is what gets repainted.
fixed.denoise: 1.0 — VAEEncodeForInpaint already restricts the change to the masked region.

fixed.upscale_method: lanczos, for the resample back down from 4x. Real-ESRGAN only produces 4x, so a request for 2x is 4x followed by a halving — which looks better than any 2x model this size would.
fixed.model: RealESRGAN_x4plus, and the reason it is the whole workflow: an upscaler is a small model and a short job, which is why this action runs on the light GPU class.

background-removal.why: No licence-clear model that can be pinned. The obvious choice, BRIA RMBG-1.4, forbids commercial use; the MIT alternative downloads its weights at first use, which cannot be hashed at build time. Both refusals are recorded in pins.json under `rejected`.
background-removal.consequence: The action stays in the catalogue because the product still intends it, and a job submitted for it fails with `model-missing` — the reason that exists for exactly this, with a retry stance of `no`. It is not silently dropped and it is not silently attempted.

$supersededComment: Workflow versions no longer mapped by any action, kept so a past result
stays explainable — 'generated with upscale v2' has to mean something a
year later, and 21.5 stores exactly that pair.
Empty today because every workflow here is at version 1. The mechanism is
not: `resolve()` loads by id AND version from the workflow directory, so
an entry listed here keeps resolving after the map has moved on. Adding a
version means writing `<id>@<n+1>.json`, pointing the action at it, and
listing the old pair here with what changed.
